newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: Kruger leaves Caymans to face Swiss fraud charges.
newsitem.headline: Kruger leaves Caymans to face Swiss fraud charges.

text.p: Swiss national Peter Kruger has left the Cayman Islands for Switzerland to face charges of bankruptcy fraud involving nearly US$272 million, the government said.
A government statement termed his departure on Thursday an extradition although he was returning voluntarily rather than facing another lengthy extradition hearing.

Kruger was originally arrested in February 1996 on an extradition warrant from Switzerland through Britain. He was discharged from that warrant in August last year on a technicality but was rearrested on a new warrant in November.
The government said this was the first local extradition under the European Convention on Extradition since it was extended to British Dependent Territories on January 15 this year.

Kruger's assets in the Cayman Islands, which total more than US$30 million, have been frozen since early 1996 when his former business partner in Switzerland, Andreas Laager, filed a civil action in the Cayman Islands.
Cayman Island's attorney general Richard Coles said that even though Kruger volunteered to return, the extradition warrant was successful.

"This demonstrates the commitment of the Cayman Islands to uphold its treaty obligations. The message we want to give is that there is no hideout in the Cayman Islands. Certainly no one should feel that he or she can escape justice by relocating to the Cayman islands."
The transfer of ownership of property linked to crime does not place assets out of reach of the law as long as they can be traced, Coles said.
Located in the western Caribbean, the Caymans are known as an off-shore financial center, tax haven and upscale tourist destination for the rich and famous.
